textbookBox.concept: Joseph Uncle's shop has toys, board games and sports items. Drawing one picture per item would take forever. So he draws one picture for every 5 items. That is a scale.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · Data Through Pictures · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A pictograph uses pictures or icons to show data.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A pictograph uses pictures or icons to show data.
beats.speakEn: A pictograph uses pictures or icons to show data.

beats.en: A scale tells us how many items one icon stands for. In Joseph Uncle's pictograph, 1 icon = 5 items.
beats.speakEn: A scale tells us how many items one icon stands for. In Joseph Uncle's pictograph, 1 icon  equals  5 items.

type: Key Concept: A pictograph uses pictures or icons to show data.
Rule: A scale tells us how many items one icon stands for.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · Data Through Pictures · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: To find a total, count the icons and multiply by the scale. 4 icons x 5 = 20 items.

beats.en: To find a total, count the icons and multiply by the scale. 4 icons x 5 = 20 items.
beats.speakEn: To find a total, count the icons and multiply by the scale. 4 icons x 5  equals  20 items.

beats.en: Deepti counted two-wheelers passing her house and used 1 icon = 3 two-wheelers. 7 icons mean 7 x 3 = 21 two-wheelers.
beats.speakEn: Deepti counted two-wheelers passing her house and used 1 icon  equals  3 two-wheelers. 7 icons mean 7 x 3  equals  21 two-wheelers.

type: To find a total, count the icons and multiply by the scale. 4 icons x 5 = 20 items.
Deepti counted two-wheelers passing her house and used 1 icon = 3 two-wheelers.

textbookBox.concept: A different scale changes the number of icons but not the data. We can choose a scale that is easy for the data, like 2, 5 or 10.
